rock-paper-scissors.description: Two-player encrypted Rock Paper Scissors game
rock-paper-scissors.title: Rock Paper Scissors
rock-paper-scissors.extraDoc:
## 🎮 How It Works

This game uses FHE to keep player moves secret until both players have committed:

1. **Player 1 creates a game** with an encrypted move (Rock=1, Paper=2, Scissors=3)
2. **Player 2 joins** with their own encrypted move
3. **Reveal phase** determines winner using encrypted comparisons

## 📊 Game Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P1 as Player 1
    participant C as Contract
    participant P2 as Player 2
    P1->>C: createGame(encryptedMove)
    Note over C: Move stored encrypted
    P2->>C: joinGame(gameId, encryptedMove)
    Note over C: Both moves encrypted
    P1->>C: revealGame(gameId)
    Note over C: FHE.select determines winner
    C-->>P1: Result decrypted for both
    C-->>P2: Result decrypted for both
```

private-age-verification.description: Verify age without revealing birthdate using FHE
private-age-verification.title: Private Age Verification
private-age-verification.extraDoc:
## 🔐 Privacy-Preserving Identity

This example shows how to prove statements about encrypted data without revealing the underlying value.

**Use Case:** Prove you are over 18 without revealing your exact birthdate.

## 📊 Verification Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Contract
    participant V as Verifier
    U->>C: registerBirthYear(encryptedYear)
    Note over C: Birth year stored encrypted
    U->>C: proveAgeTo(verifier, currentYear, minAge)
    Note over C: FHE.ge(limitYear, birthYear)
    C-->>V: ebool result allowed for verifier
    V->>V: Decrypt result (true/false)
```

## 💡 Key Insight

The verifier only learns **true or false** - never the actual birth year.

private-crowdfunding.extraDoc:
## 💰 Confidential Fundraising

Keep campaign targets and individual contributions private to:
- Prevent front-running or manipulation
- Protect contributor privacy
- Allow fair participation without social pressure

## 📊 Campaign Flow

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2

    Active --> Active: pledge(encAmount)

    Finalized --> Success: totalPledged >= target

```

fhe-counter.description: A simple FHE counter demonstrating basic encrypted operations
fhe-counter.title: Encrypted Counter
fhe-counter.extraDoc:
## 🎯 The Simplest FHE Example

This counter demonstrates the fundamental FHE operations:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Encrypt Value] --> B[Send to Contract]
    B --> C[FHE.add/sub]
    C --> D[Encrypted Result]
    D --> E[User Decrypts]
```

## 💡 What You'll Learn

- How to receive encrypted inputs with proofs
- How to perform arithmetic on encrypted values
- How to grant decryption permissions with FHE.allow

encrypt-single-value.description: Demonstrates FHE encryption mechanism and common pitfalls
encrypt-single-value.title: Encrypt Single Value
encrypt-single-value.extraDoc:
## 🔐 Understanding Encryption Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client: Generate Encrypted Input] --> B[Bound to Contract + User]
    B --> C[Send TX with handle + proof]
    C --> D[Contract: FHE.fromExternal]
    D --> E{Proof Valid?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Store euint handle]
    E -->|No| G[Revert]
```

## ⚠️ Common Pitfall

If the transaction sender doesn't match the proof signer, it will **REVERT**.

encrypt-multiple-values.extraDoc:

user-decrypt-single-value.description: Demonstrates user decryption and permission requirements
user-decrypt-single-value.title: User Decrypt Single
user-decrypt-single-value.extraDoc:
## 🔓 User Decryption (Re-encryption)

User decryption allows a specific user to decrypt a value off-chain:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Contract
    participant R as Relayer/Gateway
    U->>C: Call function
    C->>C: FHE.allow(handle, user)
    U->>R: Request re-encryption
    R-->>U: Decrypted value
```

## ⚠️ Required: FHE.allow

If you forget `FHE.allow(handle, user)`, decryption will **FAIL**.

## 🌍 Public Decryption

Make encrypted values publicly visible (e.g., game results, vote tallies):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Contract
    participant G as Gateway
    participant A as Anyone
    C->>C: FHE.makePubliclyDecryptable(handle)
    C->>G: Request decryption
    G-->>C: Callback with clear value
    A->>C: Read public result
```

fhe-operations.description: Demonstrates FHE arithmetic operations (Add, Sub, Mul)
fhe-operations.title: FHE Operations
fhe-operations.extraDoc:
## ➕ Arithmetic on Encrypted Data

| Operation | Function | Notes |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| Add | `FHE.add(a, b)` | Wraps on overflow |
| Subtract | `FHE.sub(a, b)` | Wraps on underflow |
| Multiply | `FHE.mul(a, b)` | Watch for overflow |
| Divide | `FHE.div(a, b)` | b must be non-zero |

## ⚠️ Overflow Behavior

FHE arithmetic **wraps around** like Solidity unchecked:
- `255 + 1 = 0` (for euint8)
- `0 - 1 = 255` (for euint8)

access-control.description: Demonstrates FHE.allow and FHE.allowTransient for access control
access-control.title: Access Control
access-control.extraDoc:
## 🔐 Permission System

| Function | Scope | Use Case |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `FHE.allowThis(h)` | Contract | Let contract use handle |
| `FHE.allow(h, addr)` | Persistent | Let user decrypt |
| `FHE.allowTransient(h, addr)` | This TX | Temporary access |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Handle Created] --> B{Who needs access?}
    B -->|Contract| C[FHE.allowThis]
    B -->|User| D[FHE.allow]
    B -->|Temp| E[FHE.allowTransient]
```

input-proofs.description: Shows correct usage of input proofs to prevent malling
input-proofs.title: Input Proofs
input-proofs.extraDoc:
## 🛡️ Why Input Proofs Matter

Input proofs prevent **ciphertext mauling attacks**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Attacker sees Alice's ciphertext] --> B{Try to use it?}
    B -->|Without proof| C[❌ Rejected]
    B -->|With Alice's proof| D[❌ Signature mismatch]
    B -->|With own proof| E[❌ Different ciphertext]
```

## 🔑 The Proof Binds:

1. **Ciphertext** to **Contract Address**
2. **Ciphertext** to **Sender Address**

handles.description: Explains the concept of FHE handles and their lifecycle
handles.title: Handles Lifecycle
handles.extraDoc:
## 📊 What is a Handle?

A **handle** is a 256-bit identifier pointing to encrypted data in the FHE coprocessor.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[euint32] -->|unwrap| B[bytes32 handle]
    B -->|points to| C[Encrypted Data in Coprocessor]
```

## 🔄 Handle Lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Created: FHE.fromExternal / FHE.asEuint
    Created --> Used: FHE operations
    Used --> NewHandle: Result of operation
    NewHandle --> Stored: Save to state
    Stored --> Allowed: FHE.allow/allowThis
    Allowed --> Decrypted: User/Public decrypt
```

## 💡 Key Insight

Every FHE operation creates a **NEW handle**. The original handle remains unchanged.

confidential-voting.description: Secret ballot voting where individual votes remain encrypted until the end
confidential-voting.title: Confidential Voting
confidential-voting.extraDoc:
## 🗳️ Secret Ballot Voting

Votes remain encrypted until the voting period ends:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Voter
    participant C as Contract
    participant G as Gateway
    V->>C: vote(encryptedBool)
    Note over C: yesCount += select(vote, 1, 0)
    Note over C: noCount += select(vote, 0, 1)
    C->>C: revealResult() after deadline
    C->>G: Public decryption request
    G-->>C: submitResult(proof)
    Note over C: Results now public
```

## 🔐 Privacy Guarantees

- Individual votes are **never revealed**
- Only the **final tally** is decrypted
- No one can see vote distribution during voting

blind-auction.title: Blind Auction
blind-auction.extraDoc:
## 🔨 Sealed-Bid Auction

Bids are encrypted until the auction ends:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Bidding: Auction Created
    Bidding --> Bidding: bid(encryptedAmount)
    Bidding --> Ended: stopAuction()
    Ended --> Revealed: Gateway decrypts winner
    Revealed --> Claimed: Winners claim
```

## 💡 Winner Selection

```solidity
ebool isHigher = FHE.gt(userBid, _highestBid);
_highestBid = FHE.select(isHigher, userBid, _highestBid);
```

The highest bid updates **without revealing any amounts**.

lab-input-proof.description: Interactive Lab: Learn why input proofs are bound to contracts
lab-input-proof.title: Lab: Input Proofs
lab-input-proof.extraDoc:
## 🧪 Lab Challenge

**Goal:** Understand why proofs are bound to specific contracts.

### Steps:
1. ✅ Create valid proof for Contract A
2. ❌ Try to use same proof on Contract B
3. 🔍 Observe the revert

### Learning Outcome:
Proofs contain the contract address in the signature. Using a proof on a different contract will always fail.

lab-wrong-signer.description: Security Lab: Demonstrates input binding to sender address
lab-wrong-signer.title: Lab: Wrong Signer
lab-wrong-signer.extraDoc:
## 🧪 Lab Challenge

**Goal:** Learn that proofs are bound to `msg.sender`.

### Attack Scenario:
1. Alice creates an encrypted input
2. Bob intercepts Alice's ciphertext + proof
3. Bob tries to submit it as his own

### Expected Result:
```
❌ REVERT: Proof signer != msg.sender
```

erc7984-example.title: ERC7984 Token
erc7984-example.extraDoc:
## 🪙 Confidential Token Standard

ERC7984 is the **FHE-native token standard** by OpenZeppelin:

| Feature | ERC20 | ERC7984 |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Balances | Public | Encrypted (euint64) |
| Transfers | Visible | Amounts hidden |
| Approvals | Public | Encrypted |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Public ERC20] -->|Wrap| B[Private ERC7984]
    B -->|Unwrap| A
```

erc20-wrapper.description: Wraps a public ERC20 token into a private ERC7984 token
erc20-wrapper.title: ERC20 Wrapper
erc20-wrapper.extraDoc:
## 🔄 Public to Private Bridge

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[100 USDC] -->|wrap| B[100 cUSDC]
    B -->|Transfer privately| C[Recipient]
    C -->|unwrap| D[100 USDC]
```

### Decimal Handling
Note: ERC7984 uses **6 decimals** (euint64 max ~18.4 quintillion).
Wrapping from 18-decimal ERC20 scales down by 10^12.

erc7984-erc20-swap.description: Atomic swap between ERC7984 and ERC20 tokens
erc7984-erc20-swap.title: Swap ERC7984 <-> ERC20
erc7984-erc20-swap.extraDoc:
## 🔄 Hybrid Atomic Swap

Swap private tokens for public tokens:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Alice (Seller)
    participant C as Swap Contract
    participant B as Bob (Buyer)
    A->>C: createOrder(encryptedAmount, publicPrice)
    Note over C: Lock private tokens
    B->>C: fillOrder(orderId)
    Note over C: Transfer public tokens to Alice
    Note over C: Transfer private tokens to Bob
```

erc7984-erc7984-swap.description: Atomic swap between two confidential ERC7984 tokens
erc7984-erc7984-swap.title: Swap ERC7984 <-> ERC7984
erc7984-erc7984-swap.extraDoc:
## 🔄 Fully Private Atomic Swap

Both sides of the trade remain confidential:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Alice: 100 TokenA] -->|Lock| C[Swap Contract]
    B[Bob: 200 TokenB] -->|Lock| C
    C -->|FHE.eq check| D{Amounts Match?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Swap Executes]
    D -->|No| F[Swap 0 tokens]
```

## 💡 Key Feature

Amounts are verified with `FHE.eq` - if they don't match the expected, the swap transfers nothing.

vesting-wallet.description: Confidential vesting wallet for ERC7984 tokens
vesting-wallet.title: Vesting Wallet
vesting-wallet.extraDoc:
## 📈 Confidential Linear Vesting

Vesting schedule where the **total allocation remains private**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Locked: ████████] -->|Time passes| B[Vested: ████░░░░]
    B -->|More time| C[Vested: ██████░░]
    C -->|Cliff reached| D[Fully Vested: ████████]
```

### Formula:
```
vested = totalAllocation * (currentTime - start) / duration
```

All calculated on **encrypted values**.
